newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Trieste-stored coffee has gone bad - source.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Trieste-stored coffee has gone bad - source.

text.p: Brazilian coffee stored in Trieste, Italy, for 10 years awaiting the outcome of a court decision has gone bad and its release to the market will have no effect on prices, local market sources said.
"The coffee is very bad. It is so old that it will have virtually no use," said a Brazilian exporter, who asked not to be named.

The coffee, which is more than fifteen years old and was poorly stored, is expected to be used in very small quantities, no more than 10 percent of the total blend in the soluble industry, the source said.

In July, a European court ruled Brazil must compensate companies for losses in the so-called Patricia Operation in 1986. The operation was masterminded by the Brazilian government to hike coffee prices.

It involved the buying of futures contracts for 600,000 60-kg bags of coffee from London's terminal market by 18 firms. Under the scheme, some of the coffee would return to Brazil to supply the domestic market and the remainder would be re-sold at higher prices in Europe. The plan included using the coffee to build strategic stockpiles around Europe, one of them in Trieste.
The idea was to maximize Brazil's revenue from its coffee exports which were sharply down that year due to drought.
